key_insight: Reactive sputtering can produce epitaxial Mn4N thin films with strong perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and current-driven switching, making them promising for spintronic devices.
engineering_relevance: The work identifies scalable growth conditions for rare-earth-free Mn4N films that combine robust magnetic anisotropy, large anomalous Hall response, and efficient spin-orbit torque functionality.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of Mn4N on MgO(100) and SrTiO3(100) substrates
Structural, magnetic, and magnetotransport characterization of film quality and anisotropy
Density functional theory to assess the roles of strain and interfaces in PMA
evidence_signal: The optimized epitaxial films show square hysteresis loops, high remanence, tunable coercivity, pronounced anomalous Hall effect, and current-induced switching in Mn4N/Pt bilayers.
watch_item: PMA is influenced not only by epitaxial strain but also by interfacial effects, so device performance may depend sensitively on substrate and interface engineering.
paper_title: Optimization of Epitaxial Mn4N Thin Films Grown by Sputtering for Spintronic Applications
